channel.title: Willis Strategy Group — Insights
channel.description: Articles, book reviews, and the weekly Defense Dispatch from Willis Strategy Group.

item.title: Defense Dispatch — Issue 02
item.description: Columbus–Chattahoochee Valley defense innovation & investment, every week. Issue 02 — GM Defense’s $700M ISV contract, the Battle Lab’s tethered drones, and CMI2 at the Maneuver Warfighter Conference.

item.title: The MWI Pacific Papers
item.description: West Point’s 2026 collection on deterring China by denying a quick victory — a contest for time, and where the land force fits.

item.title: Defense Dispatch
item.description: Columbus–Chattahoochee Valley defense innovation & investment, every week. Issue 01 — SBIR Release 6, CMI2, and Hanwha’s $262M Army contract.

item.title: World War II with Tom Hanks
item.description: The twenty-hour HISTORY Channel series as command education and a study in strategic communication — the map before the terrain walk of the campaign histories.

item.title: The Visionaries — James Holland
item.description: How the postwar order was deliberately engineered — Bretton Woods, the Marshall Plan, and the long-horizon leadership that built eighty years of peace on purpose.

item.title: The Arms of the Future — Jack Watling
item.description: Why ubiquitous sensors and precision fires may have made twentieth-century maneuver doctrine obsolete — and a research agenda for the force that must replace it.

item.title: Ground Combat Element 2040 — USMC
item.description: The Marine Corps' human-centric framework for future ground forces — five pillars, a phased path to 2040, and the experimentation that will decide whether it holds.

item.title: Donovan’s Devils — Albert Lulushi
item.description: The OSS Operational Groups — immigrant soldiers who became the forerunners of Army Special Forces — and a founding case study in building capability from nothing.

item.title: The Spurs of Service — Jacob P. Kelly
item.description: A cavalry officer’s poems on service, loss, and the long ride home — and why a leader’s emotional honesty may be the most protective example he can set.

item.title: Victory ’45 — Holland & Murray
item.description: The eight surrenders that ended the Second World War — and the case-study anthology in conflict termination that every leader who plans operations without planning endings should read.

item.title: The Allies Strike Back — James Holland
item.description: The War in the West, Vol. 2: how coalition machinery, operational research, and honest after-action learning turned the tide from 1941 to 1943.

item.title: The Rise of Germany — James Holland
item.description: The War in the West, Vol. 1: why the Wehrmacht's early victories concealed fatal weakness — and what net assessment misses without the logistics ledger.

item.title: Cassino ’44 — James Holland
item.description: Monte Cassino, Anzio, and the liberation of Rome — the brutal conclusion of the Italian Campaign trilogy, and its lessons for sustained large-scale combat operations.

item.title: Dam Busters — James Holland
item.description: Operation Chastise as a case study in rapid capability development: from unproven concept to war-changing raid in under ten weeks — and the leadership that made it possible.

item.title: Pacific Blitzkrieg — Sharon Tosi Lacey
item.description: How the Army and Marine Corps forged joint ground operations across five Central Pacific invasions — and why integration is forged by leaders, not declared by doctrine.

item.title: A Hybrid Approach to Combat Simulation Experimentation
item.description: Combining human-in-the-loop and closed-loop constructive simulation to capture the strengths of both — real-world applicability and statistical significance — in warfighting experiments.

item.title: A Framework for the Accreditation of Simulation-Based Experiments
item.description: Who accredits your experiments? A cross-functional framework for accrediting the entire simulation experiment — models, scenario, environment, and analysis — not just the M&S.

item.title: George Marshall: Defender of the Republic — David L. Roll
item.description: The Army's greatest soldier-statesman as a field manual for leader development: talent management as a weapon system, candor as a career strategy, selflessness as strategic capital.

item.title: Project Maven — Katrina Manson
item.description: The story of the Maven Smart System, reviewed through a Battle Lab lens: what a decade of AI-warfare development teaches about experimentation, iteration, and fielding capability under friction.

item.title: Sicily ’43 — James Holland
item.description: Operation Husky and the first assault on Fortress Europe — timeless lessons on Joint Forcible Entry Operations, airborne fragility, and air and naval superiority.

item.title: The Savage Storm — James Holland
item.description: Salerno and the battle for Italy, 1943 — what an infantry-centric slog against a determined defender teaches the modern student of large-scale combat operations.

item.title: Brothers in Arms — James Holland
item.description: The Sherwood Rangers' transformation from horse cavalry to legendary tank regiment — and its lessons for the Army Transformation Initiative.
